newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Degussa upbeat for 96/97, share price soars.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Degussa upbeat for 96/97, share price soars.

text.p: German chemicals and metals group Degussa AG on Monday delivered an optimistic outlook for its current business year, which revved up the share price, and also reported a two percent profit rise in 1995/1996.
The current business year had started strongly and the marked improvement in business in recent months, particularly in Europe, will likely continue, Degussa said in a statement.
"We expect that the positive trend will be maintained in 1996/1997," the group said.
The outlook, more than the results, let Degussa shares climb nearly four percent to 663 marks in Frankfurt bourse trade and laid the groundwork for still more spectacular gains, analysts said.

"Since results were in line with expectations, it is the outlook and Degussa's increased emphasis on shareholder value, including the willingness to restructure poor performers, that helped drive share prices higher," said Christa Baehr, analyst at Bankgesellschaft Berlin in Berlin.
She forecast shares may climb to 750 to 800 marks in the coming months and said the forecast rise may accelerate as Degussa polishes up its image and promises ever better results.

In the 1995/1996 business year, ending on September 30, Degussa reported a two percent rise in pre-tax profits to 413 million marks, marking a second consecutive record result. Earnings per share advanced to 39 marks from 38.
Sales however dipped one percent to 13.79 billion marks. Adjusted for changes in the consolidated group and in precious metals trading, group sales fell two percent, Degussa said.

Degussa, like other German chemical companies, felt the full impact of a slump in prices coupled with sluggish economic conditions, which were particularly pronounced in Germany, in late 1995 and early 1996.
Mirroring its rivals' geographically mixed results, Degussa said sales growth came primarily from North and Latin America, with Europe showing only a small rise while German sales fell.

Since then Degussa has initiated a number of restructuring programmes and hinted it will not tolerate non-performing units, leaving analysts delighted with newly appointed chief executive Uwe-Ernst Bufe's style. He replaced Gert Becker who retired this year.

The company reported its 1995/96 results based on a reorganised management structure with the three divisions chemical products, health and nutrition, and precious metals and bank activities. Year-earlier results have been made comparable.
Among the group's three core business areas, health and nutrition, which Degussa plans to build up over the next years, posted a two percent rise in sales to 2.69 billion marks.

Degussa's Asta Medica group, fresh from purchasing U.S.-based Muro Pharmaceuticals, "posted satisfying results," the group said, adding strong earnings were posted by the dental and feed additives products.
Asta Medica in September raised its stake in Muro to 100 percent from the 20 percent stake bought earlier in this year.
Degussa's chemical sector sales were flat at 3.84 billion marks in 1995/1996 compared with 3.85 a year earlier but it posted a strong rise in earnings, the group said.

Sales in Degussa's largest business sector, precious metals and banking, fell two percent to 7.25 billion marks. Earnings in the sector, impacted by restructuring costs and provisions for the precious metals and auto catalysts divisions, were also not satisfactory, the group said.
Analysts were confident however that the new management would not tolerate drains on earnings for long and may consider spinning off certain units.
